definition: Elude means to evade or escape.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word elude. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know elude should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The counterfeiter eluded auditors for years by keeping two sets of books in two different languages.
Dodge is a smaller act than elude — a single sidestep around one grab, one question, one puddle — while eluding means slipping away again and again, for as long as the hunt lasts.
Vanish goes further than elude: the quarry is not merely uncaught but gone without trace, as if it had never been there.

Evade is elude's near twin — slipping away by cunning — but it leans toward duties, taxes, and questions: you evade responsibility or a direct answer. Elude is the broader escape-artist's word: pursuers, nets, cures, even a name on the tip of your tongue can elude you.

To outrun is to beat pursuers by sheer speed — a footrace you win. Elude wins by quickness and cunning instead: slipping away, doubling back, staying out of sight. A fugitive can elude a manhunt for years without ever once outrunning anybody.

To shake is to break free of pursuers who are actively on your tail — the cruiser behind you, the reporter at your heels. Elude is wider and quieter: you elude searchers who never even find you. You can only shake what has found you.
